summary.headline: Gopal Snacks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 409.6 cr; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% with Rajkot plant fully commissioned.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 409.6 crore, up 29% YoY and 2.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 31.5 crore (7.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 29.9 crore (7.3% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 2.7% to Rs 1,508.2 crore, EBITDA was Rs 101.3 crore (6.7%) and PAT Rs 73.7 crore (4.9%). Management said supply was restored after the fire-related disruption, with Rajkot commissioned (installed capacity 1,05,000 MT) and the Modasa plant fully integrated. Insurance receipts reached about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26, with a further claim expected to be settled around Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 17.5 crore in Q4; about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26

segments.name: Gathiya
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 410 crore; FY27 growth target 18-20%. Management estimates Gujarat Gathiya industry growth at 15-20%.

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 350 crore; FY27 growth target 15%. Gujarat Namkeen industry growth estimated at 14-15%.

segments.name: Fryums / Pellets
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 250 crore; FY27 growth target 15%, in line with industry.

segments.name: Wafers
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 155 crore; FY27 growth target 40%.

segments.name: Others (papad, besan, spices, bakery, noodles, rusk)
segments.commentary: FY27 growth target of 30%. New products (kaju biscuit, popcorn) grew from Rs 25 crore to Rs 63 crore in FY26, with about Rs 50 crore of the Rs 38 crore delta from core states (as stated).

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% on an annualised average basis; exit run-rate expected near double digit.

FY27 incremental revenue target of Rs 330-350 crore: Rs 170-180 crore from core market (Gujarat), Rs 125-130 crore from focus states, Rs 35 crore from other states, quick commerce, railways and modern trade.
Advertisement spend projected at 2.2-2.3% of revenue in FY27 versus about 1.7% in FY26; trade spend cuts to be gradual, not major in FY27.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 40-45 crore, including a corporate office building at Rajkot; the rest is maintenance.
Finance cost expected to be slightly higher in FY27, about Rs 10 crore versus about Rs 7 crore in FY26.
Insurance balance claim expected to be Rs 35-40 crore (higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, as restatement cost exceeds WDV write-off), with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajkot plant commissioned; installed capacity 1,05,000 MT. Gondal facility to be discontinued.
Plant roles: Rajkot makes gathiya, namkeen, snack pellets and extruded snacks; Modasa makes all namkeen and wafers; Nagpur makes gathiya, namkeen, pellets and wafers.
Third-party manufacturing used in Kashipur (UP; four SKUs making 76-77% of UP sales) and Chhattisgarh (wafers only) to cut transport costs in those markets.
FY27 capacity utilisation expected at about 43-45%, per management in response to a question; Q4 utilisation near the full-year level shown on slide 11.
demand_pricing: Core market (Gujarat) run-rate about Rs 85-90 crore per month; about 300 distributors; line-wide coverage at 29% of beats on twice-a-week service by end-Q4, targeting 40% by end-Q1 FY27.
Focus states run-rate about Rs 400 crore annualised across 600 distributors; 65-70 dealers added in Q4 and 69 new distributors in Q4 against an annual target of 250.
Per-day run-rate has improved since March; Uttar Pradesh H2 was 26% above H1; monthly UP sales about Rs 6.5 crore with 72% from two SKUs, target exit Rs 8.5-9 crore.
Grammage cut of about 4% taken in mid-April 2026 on small packs, with price hikes on larger SKUs; further action depends on competitor response.
Raw material basket: palm oil 26-27%, chana 21-22%, laminate 18-19%, potato about 6%. RM inflation impact about 4-4.5% so far, largely offset by grammage cuts, price increases and BOM changes.
Chana stock sufficient to about November 2026; H2 purchases to be made from market or imports if cheaper.
Distributor count 953 at end-Q4 versus 884 at end-Q3; 97% of business through direct distributors; DMS live at 90% of dealers.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 top line shape up now that supply is restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore revenue delta in FY27: Rs 170-180 crore core Gujarat, Rs 125-130 crore focus states, Rs 35 crore other channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did focus states grow more slowly than core states in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Core states were hit harder by the fire, depleting the base. Q4 beat Q3 this year, reversing the usual 6-7% seasonal dip, and focus-state growth is expected to rebuild on distributor additions. Growth is expected at par near term and higher on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held the 8-9% average guidance, citing raw material volatility. Exit run-rate is expected near double digit. Trade spend will be cut only gradually, with no major cut in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much more insurance will be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance claim expected at Rs 35-40 crore, higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher chana inventory bought ahead of expected price rises raised bank borrowing. Receivable days rose by 9 days, but the working capital cycle is within the comfort zone.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut prices or pack sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4% grammage cut was taken in mid-April 2026. Further action depends on how the industry responds.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation in palm oil and packaging (cited as 15-20% basket increase); H2 FY27 chana purchases exposed to pulse prices, with El Nino raising rain-deficit risk to rural demand.
Unorganised Rs 5 price-point players under pressure; no action seen yet. Industry pricing discipline may change.
Insurance balance claim timing (Q2 FY27 expected) and asset restatement progress.
Focus-state growth recovery and distributor additions versus the target of 250 for CY26.
Rising debt and finance cost (about Rs 10 crore expected in FY27) on higher inventory.
Trade spend and advertising step-up (2.2-2.3% of revenue) could compress margins if market-share recovery needs more spend.
summary.management_tone: Confident and specific on recovery metrics, distributor adds and capacity; more cautious and hedged on margin drivers and raw material inflation, with the 8-9% margin guidance held despite analyst pressure to raise it. Some answers were vague on pricing and on how industry players will react.

Rigan Raithatha: So, as far as trade spend is concerned, we would be obviously looking on that front but that our reduction on the trade spend would be in a very gradual phase wise manner.

adds.what: Rajkot plant fully commissioned; installed capacity 1,05,000 MT (Gondal facility to be discontinued)

growth.why: FY27 incremental revenue target of Rs 330-350 crore (about 22-23% on FY26 Rs 1,508 crore) backed by distributor expansion (953 distributors, focus-state run-rate ~Rs 400 cr) and segment targets, but no firm order book; Rajkot capacity is already live with utilisation only ~43-45%, so the delivery case rests on demand gains rather than new capacity.
